adjustments.description: Settlement of a commercial dispute. Non-recurring.
adjustments.management_rationale: Settlement of commercial dispute - non-recurring. Management advises this relates to a separate matter from FY2023 and FY2024 settlements.
adjustments.reasoning: The identical settlement category, identical amount ($2,100,000), and identical rationale ('Settlement of commercial dispute - non-recurring') appear in each of FY2023 (ADJ-001), FY2024 (ADJ-002), and FY2025 (ADJ-003). Board Minutes (DOC-09, Item 7) explicitly state: 'the third annual settlement under the ongoing series of commercial disputes with former channel partners had been concluded at $2.1M, consistent with the prior two years. The Board asked whether provision should be made for a further settlement in FY2026.' This is contemporaneous board-level evidence that the settlements form an ongoing series, not isolated non-recurring events. The CFO's own characterisation ('matters are being treated as non-recurring for the purposes of the sale process') confirms the non-recurring label is a sale-process presentation choice, not an independent factual determination. Three consecutive years of identical amounts constitutes a recurring economic pattern. The add-back is rejected as inappropriate for normalized historical EBITDA.

existence.detail: Settlement confirmed by Board Minutes Item 7 (DOC-09). Economic event is real.

amount.detail: Amount of $2,100,000 consistent across structured data (mgmt_ebitda_adjustment), QoE schedule (DOC-08), and Board Minutes (DOC-09).

period.detail: Board Minutes dated 22 October 2025 confirm FY2025 settlement concluded.

recurrence.detail: SQL-EV-003 and SQL-EV-013: Identical category, identical amount ($2,100,000) in FY2023, FY2024, and FY2025. Three consecutive years. Board Minutes explicitly describe 'third annual settlement under the ongoing series of commercial disputes.' Board asked about FY2026 provision.

duplication.detail: Each year's settlement is a separate row. No duplication within FY2025.

underlying_data.detail: Structured data shows three consecutive identical adjustments. No structured data contradicts the existence of the settlement, but the pattern contradicts the non-recurring classification.

document_support.detail: Board Minutes (DOC-09, Item 7) describe an 'ongoing series' of disputes and a third annual settlement. The CFO's own statement that matters are 'being treated as non-recurring for the purposes of the sale process' is an explicit acknowledgement that the non-recurring label is a sale-process choice, not an independent factual determination.

adjustments.description: Trading losses on the Legacy On-Prem product, which is being sunset.
adjustments.management_rationale: Losses on Legacy On-Prem product being sunset.
adjustments.reasoning: The Legacy On-Prem product family (PRD-016: Legacy On-Prem Licence, PRD-017: Legacy Maintenance) exists in the product master (dim_product). However, SQL-EV-008 and SQL-EV-022 confirm zero invoice line revenue for both Legacy products across all periods in the structured data — no Legacy product revenue appears in fact_invoice_line for any year. SQL-EV-023 confirms FY2025 revenue is entirely from Platform, Professional Services, and Managed Services product families, with no Legacy family revenue. This means the structured data neither confirms nor independently quantifies the $540,000 loss amount — the absence of Legacy revenue in invoice lines could indicate the product has already ceased generating revenue, or that losses are cost-side (hosting, support, maintenance costs) not captured in the revenue tables. No VDR document provides a formal discontinuation commitment, board resolution, sunset timeline, or cost schedule for the Legacy On-Prem product. The QoE schedule asserts the product 'is being sunset' but no authoritative document confirms this commitment or establishes when costs will cease. The adjustment cannot be accepted (no formal discontinuation commitment or cost evidence) but cannot be rejected (the product exists, losses may be real cost-side items, and discontinuation is plausible). Verdict: Challenged. Accepted amount: null — no independently supportable amount can be quantified without an unsupported assumption about the cost composition of the $540,000 loss.

adjustments.category: Pro-forma full-year effect of new logos
adjustments.description: Annualising the FY2025 in-year contribution of logos won during the year.
adjustments.reasoning: Step 1 — Underlying Event: SQL-EV-005 confirms 20 customers with first_order_date >= 2025-01-01 invoiced in FY2025, with total FY2025 invoiced revenue of $1,878,956. The underlying new logo events are real. Step 2 — Timing: New logos were won throughout FY2025 (January through December), with varying partial-year contributions. Step 3 — Continuation/Commitment: SQL-EV-015 shows contracts for new FY2025 logos. Cascade Foods Holdings (CUST-0006) has an executed MSA (CTR-00006, ACV $1,950,000, contract start 2025-06-01, end 2028-05-31, auto-renew Y, status Active) — this is the strongest contractual commitment. However, several other new logos have contracts with start dates predating their first_order_date, expired contracts, or contracts with no auto-renew, raising questions about the reliability of annualisation for the full cohort. Step 4 — Overlap/Double Counting: CUST-0006 (Cascade Foods Holdings) has parent_customer_id = CUST-0005 (Cascade Foods). SQL-EV-021 shows Cascade Foods (CUST-0005) revenue declined from $1,972,869 in FY2024 to $407,201 in FY2025, while Cascade Foods Holdings (CUST-0006) generated $1,206,022 in FY2025. The combined FY2025 revenue of both entities ($1,613,223) is broadly consistent with Cascade Foods' prior-year revenue ($1,972,869), suggesting CUST-0006 may represent a corporate restructuring or re-engagement of an existing economic relationship rather than a genuinely new logo. This creates a material overlap risk for the annualisation. Step 5 — Verdict: The adjustment is Challenged. The underlying new logo events are real and some contractual commitment exists (particularly for Cascade Foods Holdings). However, the annualisation methodology is assumption-dependent (requires assumed run-rate continuation for each logo), the Cascade Foods Holdings/Cascade Foods relationship creates a material overlap risk, and the management amount of $1,650,000 cannot be independently reconstructed from authoritative evidence without unsupported assumptions. Accepted amount: null — no independently supportable annualised amount can be quantified without assuming run-rate continuation for each logo, which is not established by authoritative evidence for the full cohort.

existence.detail: SQL-EV-005: 20 new logo customers with first_order_date >= 2025-01-01 invoiced in FY2025. Total FY2025 invoiced revenue $1,878,956. Underlying new logo events are real.

amount.detail: Management's $1,650,000 annualisation amount cannot be independently reconstructed. Total new logo FY2025 invoiced revenue is $1,878,956 (SQL-EV-007). The annualisation methodology (partial-period to full-year) requires assumed run-rate continuation for each logo, which is not established by authoritative evidence for the full cohort. The management amount is less than total FY2025 invoiced revenue, suggesting management may have applied a partial-year uplift to a subset of logos, but the methodology is not documented.

period.detail: New logos won in FY2025 with partial-year contributions. Annualisation concept is period-appropriate but methodology is undocumented.

recurrence.detail: No pro-forma new logo adjustment in FY2023 or FY2024 structured data.

duplication.detail: SQL-EV-021: Cascade Foods Holdings (CUST-0006, parent = CUST-0005 Cascade Foods) generated $1,206,022 in FY2025 while Cascade Foods (CUST-0005) declined from $1,972,869 (FY2024) to $407,201 (FY2025). Combined FY2025 revenue of both entities ($1,613,223) is broadly consistent with Cascade Foods prior-year revenue, suggesting CUST-0006 may represent a re-engagement of an existing economic relationship. DOC-06 (Cascade Foods Holdings MSA) notes a 2025 re-engagement after lapse of a prior agreement. This creates a material overlap risk: treating CUST-0006 as a new logo may overstate the genuine new logo contribution.

underlying_data.detail: SQL-EV-005: 20 new logos, $1,878,956 FY2025 invoiced. SQL-EV-015: Contracts exist for new logos; Cascade Foods Holdings has strongest commitment (ACV $1,950,000, active, auto-renew). SQL-EV-017: Total new logo ACV $2,832,316 (Cascade Holdings $1,950,000; others $882,316). SQL-EV-018: Cascade Foods Holdings ARR active from June 2025 at ~$1,600,000-$1,629,017. Other new logos have smaller and less certain ARR profiles. SQL-EV-014: New logo FY2025 revenue excluding Cascade Holdings = $672,934 across 19 customers.

document_support.detail: DOC-06 (Cascade Foods Holdings MSA, CTR-00006): Executed agreement, ACV $1,950,000, start 2025-06-01, end 2028-05-31, auto-renew. Strongest contractual support for one logo. DOC-06 notes re-engagement after lapse of prior agreement — raises overlap question. No executed contracts in data room for the other 19 new logos beyond the dim_contract records.

adjustments.what_would_raise_confidence: Management's annualisation methodology schedule showing which logos were included, their partial-period revenue, and the annualisation basis for each. Confirmation of whether Cascade Foods Holdings is treated as a new logo or a continuation of the Cascade Foods relationship. Executed contracts for all 20 new logos confirming committed ACV. Evidence that Cascade Foods (CUST-0005) revenue decline is unrelated to the CUST-0006 re-engagement.

data_quality.description: Legacy product family (PRD-016, PRD-017) exists in dim_product but has zero invoice line revenue in fact_invoice_line across all periods. This prevents independent verification of the ADJ-007 loss amount. The absence may reflect that losses are cost-side items not captured in revenue tables, or that the product has already ceased generating revenue.

No cost or expense structured data is available in the schema (no cost table, P&L table, or expense table). This prevents independent reconstruction of reported EBITDA from structured data and limits the ability to verify cost-side adjustments (ADJ-005, ADJ-007).

Several management-referenced supporting documents are not available in the data room: (1) Third-party compensation benchmark (Sep-2025) for ADJ-004; (2) Executive search invoices for ADJ-009; (3) Sell-side adviser engagement letter/invoice for ADJ-006; (4) Settlement agreements for ADJ-001/ADJ-002/ADJ-003.
